title: Fund the most value within one budget

blocks.text: We have $38.39M of capital for the next five years and 40 candidate projects on GridCap small. Tell us which to fund to get the most value. Use the NPV finance quoted for each project. We'll worry about years later.

The project you start from is the skeleton: it reads the export and prints a report, but its model is empty and `solve` funds nothing. Make the planner decide. Each project is a yes-or-no choice, the funded projects together may cost no more than the capital budget, and the plan has the most total value. Solve the model with HiGHS through MathOpt, keep anything HiGHS prints out of the report, and read the answer back as a `Plan` in which each funded project starts in its earliest year.
The command line, `python -m cipt EXPORT.json`, plans the export file it is given.

`cipt/solve.py` already imports MathOpt and holds stubs for `run_highs` and `read_plan`; write their bodies and make `solve` use them. `cipt/report.py` needs no change. It prints the report in this format, every amount in whole $k with thousands commas:

items: `funded <n> of <all> projects, capex $<capex>k of $<capital budget>k, value $<value>k`, where capex and value are the totals of the funded projects;

one line per funded project, in id order: two spaces, the id, two spaces, `start <year>`, two spaces, `capex` and a space and the capex right-aligned in 6 characters, two spaces, `value` and a space and the value right-aligned in 6 characters, two spaces, the project's name.

blocks.text: Run executes `main.py`, which plans the demo export in `data/demo.json` (GridCap tiny, a fictional utility) and prints the report; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the skeleton's own included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.

items: **Contract.** Takes a Request. Returns a Built holding a MathOpt model with one binary variable per project (named `x_<id>`), one row named budget that keeps the summed capex of the funded projects within capital_budget, and the summed value of the funded projects as the objective to maximize.
**Modeling idea.** A yes-or-no choice per project under one budget is a 0-1 knapsack: the best fill is a combination, which no sort by value per dollar finds in general.
**Contract.** Solves the model with HiGHS through MathOpt, on one thread, and returns the SolveResult. Nothing HiGHS prints may reach the program's standard output.
**Modeling idea.** The solver is a call with parameters; its log is not the planner's report.

blocks.text: def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan

items: **Contract.** Turns a SolveResult into a Plan: the status in lower case, each project whose variable is 1 mapped to its earliest start year, and the objective value. With no feasible solution, a Plan with the status alone.
**Modeling idea.** Read the termination first, then the variable values; a binary is 1 when its value is above 0.5.

**Taught in** [4.2.2 Reading `SolveResult`: Termination, Primal and Dual Solutions, Statistics](../../../../04-google-or-tools-in-depth/13-mathopt-core/units/unit-02/4.2.2-reading-solveresult-termination-primal-and-dual-solutions-statistics.unit.html).
**Contract.** Builds the model for a Request, solves it and returns the Plan.
**Modeling idea.** Keep building, solving and reading back in separate functions, so each can be tested and changed alone.

**Taught in** [14.2.1 The First Request: Fund Projects Within One Budget](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-01/14.2.1-the-first-request-fund-projects-within-one-budget.unit.html).

"""CIPT planner: which capital projects to fund, grown one planner request at a time.

The data it ships with (data/demo.json) is GridCap, a fictional utility invented for this course.
"""

"""python -m cipt EXPORT.json: plan the export and print the report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from .data import read_request
from .report import render
from .solve import solve


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cipt", description="Plan a capital portfolio.")
    parser.add_argument("export", help="the planning export, a JSON file")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    request = read_request(args.export)
    print(render(request, solve(request)))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""The plan as the planners read it."""

from __future__ import annotations

from .data import Request
from .plan import Plan


def render(request: Request, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"{request.name}: {plan.status}"]
    funded = [request.project(pid) for pid in plan.funded]
    capex = sum(p.capex for p in funded)
    value = sum(p.value for p in funded)
    lines.append(f"funded {len(funded)} of {len(request.projects)} projects, "
                 f"capex ${capex:,}k of ${request.capital_budget:,}k, value ${value:,}k")
    for p in funded:
        lines.append(f"  {p.project_id}  start {plan.starts[p.project_id]}  "
                     f"capex {p.capex:>6,}  value {p.value:>6,}  {p.name}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Solve a request with HiGHS and read the answer back as a Plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt
from ortools.math_opt.solvers import highs_pb2

from .data import Request
from .model import Built, build
from .plan import Plan

#: One thread, set in HiGHS's own options; the first HiGHS solve of a process fixes the count.
PARAMS = mathopt.SolveParameters(highs=highs_pb2.HighsOptionsProto(int_options={"threads": 1}))


def run_highs(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with stdout pointed at /dev/null, so HiGHS's stray C output stays out of reports."""
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=PARAMS)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def read_plan(built: Built, result: mathopt.SolveResult) -> Plan:
    """Turn a solver result into a Plan; a funded project starts in its earliest year."""
    status = result.termination.reason.name.lower()
    if not result.has_primal_feasible_solution():
        return Plan(status=status)
    values = result.variable_values()
    starts = {pid: built.request.project(pid).earliest_start
              for pid, var in built.x.items() if values[var] > 0.5}
    return Plan(status=status, starts=starts, objective=result.objective_value())


def solve(request: Request) -> Plan:
    built = build(request)
    return read_plan(built, run_highs(built.model))

"""The planning export, read into typed records.

The planners' export carries every column the planning system keeps (cost profiles, windows,
rules, NPV by start year, asset health). This version reads only the columns it uses and ignores
the rest, so the same export file serves every version of the planner.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    """One candidate project, as this version of the planner sees it."""

    project_id: str
    name: str
    capex: int            # $k, the whole cost over the project's life
    value: int            # $k, the NPV finance quotes for a start in the earliest year
    earliest_start: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Request:
    """What the planners ask for: the projects, and the money to fund them with."""

    name: str
    capital_budget: int   # $k, one envelope for the whole plan
    projects: tuple[Project, ...]

    def project(self, project_id: str) -> Project:
        for p in self.projects:
            if p.project_id == project_id:
                return p
        raise KeyError(project_id)


def load_request(raw: dict) -> Request:
    """Build a Request from the export's dictionary form, refusing duplicate project ids."""
    projects = tuple(
        Project(
            project_id=row["id"],
            name=row["name"],
            capex=sum(row["cost_profile"]),
            value=row["npv"][str(row["earliest_start"])],
            earliest_start=row["earliest_start"],
        )
        for row in raw["projects"]
    )
    ids = [p.project_id for p in projects]
    if len(set(ids)) != len(ids):
        raise ValueError("duplicate project ids in the export")
    return Request(name=raw["name"], capital_budget=raw["capital_budget"], projects=projects)


def read_request(path: str | Path) -> Request:
    """Read an export file (JSON) into a Request."""
    return load_request(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
